doc.title: Joe LaBarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 15, 2021

title: The state of the country and what angers him
summary: Joe speaks of optimism tempered by worry, and anger at injustice, lies, inequality and homelessness.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: Excellent. What’s your feeling about, this is a large question, the state of our country at the moment?

Well at the moment I tend to be very optimistic. But you and I both know that lying in the weeds is something very evil and something that if we’re not mindful of is going to come right back and rear its ugly head and be right in our faces again. So to that end we’re doing what we can do to support people that we feel are going to help take us in the right direction, keep us in the right direction.
Is there anything in particular either musically or in life in general that makes you angry?

Angry, well yes of course. You know injustice makes me incredibly angry, and to hear lies being said over and over again and believed by 70 million? How many people was it? I don’t even want to — I really hate to go there but the number of people that are fooled by the lies that are being told, that makes me angry. To see blatant disregard for rule of law, that makes me very angry. To see money being siphoned to the top exclusively and then to have to go outside and drive around and see homelessness in numbers that you can’t even imagine. It’s staggering. That makes me angry. To realize that people are hungry, that makes me angry. We have so much wealth in this nation and the inequity of all of that, it gets me going.
